Seuman Sentenced.

label: text
text: A seuman was sentenced to three months' imprisonment with hard labour at Greenwich for urging a big crowd to set about the Police.

label: text
text: Three others were sentenced to terms ranging from one month to two months.

label: text
text: The Trades Union Congress announces that the International Federation of Trade Unions has requested all the centres to open relief funds for the British strikers. The Dutch Federation sent a first contribution of 25,000.

label: text
text: Cases were heard at the London, Nuneaton, Middlesborough, Chesterfield, and Newcastle Police. Courts of rioting, Impeding the Police and circulating false news.

label: text
text: The sentences ranged from a month to three months' imprisonment with hard labour.

label: text
text: Union Secretary Sentenced.

label: text
text: Alexander Auld, the local Secretary of the General Workers' Union at Shap, a small town. 12 miles south-east of Penrith, Westmorland, was sentenced to three months' imprisonment with hard labour for issuing appeals to the workers not to join the special constabulary.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAILWAY ACCIDENTS

label: paragraph_title
text: First Since Strike Commerce.

label: text
text: A passenger train at Edinburgh crushed into a stationary passenger train at Bishop-Storford (a market town 12 miles north-east of Hertford, one person being killed and another injured).

label: text
text:
An express from Edinburgh was derided north of Newcastle. There were no fatalities, but one passenger was seriously injured.
Foul Plav.

label: text
text: The British "Gazette" says that the derailment of an express from Edinburgh is believed to be due to foul play by the strikers as a fishplate had been removed.

label: text
text: There were.500 passengers on board, but only one was injured in the leg.

label: text
text: The "Gazette" says that "bolts were removed from the line near a level crossing at Egham on Sunday.

label: paragraph_title
text: Almost Normal Transport of

label: text
text: London, May 10.

label: text
text: An official communique says that the situation all over the country is well maintained.

label: text
text: The arrangements for the distribution of milk, food, and petrol were more successful than on any other day of the strike, and promise to improve continuously.

label: text
text: The unloading and transportation of commodities are approaching normality.

label: text
text: It may generally be stated that the Government emergency arrangements have settled down and are working thoroughly.

label: text
text: The position regarding the supply of light and power is satisfactory.

label: text
text: The railway services have improved. One-fifth of the regular staffs of the railway companies are working.

label: text
text: Disturbances are few, but where they have occurred they show signs of becoming sharper. Nevertheless there is no cause for anxiety and the Police have complete control.

label: paragraph_title
text: ARCHBISHOP'S APPEAL.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, arising out of a question as to the Government provisionally commandeering news print, which Mr. Winston Churchill ascribed to the necessity for safeguarding the dissemination of news throughout the country, Mr. D. Lloyd George called attention to the refusal of the broadcasting authorities to issue the appeal signed by the Archbishop of Canterbury formulated at Lambeth on Friday on behalf of the Christian Churches of the country embodying a resolution that the time for conciliation had arrived and suggesting that the general strike be

label: text
text: uncelled, that the Government offers assistance to the coal industry for a definite period by renewed, and that the mine owners' notices be withdrawn. Mr. Lloyd George complained that the foregoing appeal was not published in the British "Gazette." Mr. Winston Churchill pointed out that many important things had performed to be omitted, which the Government did not object to inserting. The Chancellor gave an assurance that the Archbishop's appeal would be inserted in the British "Gazette" at the earliest possible.

Belfast, May 10.
The Belfast dockers have struck

label: text
text: Unions' Appeal Disregarded.

label: text
text: Owing to the strike in Great Britain the bunkering stations near Rotterdam, which are "worked" by unorganised labour, are most active and the men have so far completely disrogarded the appeal of the Trade Unions to refuse to bunker British vessels.

label: text
text: Last week 78 vessels bunkered compared with 18 in the previous week.

label: text
text: French Ban.

label: text
text:
Paris, May 10.
In conformity with the Ostend decisions the National Federations of Maritime Unions of Port and Dock Labourers have issued instructions forbidding unemployed seamen to serve on British ships.
French seamen refuse to work on French coal ships bound for Great Britain, and are ordering dockers not to coal or victual British vessels.

label: paragraph_title
text: Danish Subscription

label: text
text: The Danish Trade Union Congress has decided to send the British Trade Unions 50,000 kroner weekly so long as the strike lasts.

label: text
text: NO FRESH DEVELOPMENT

label: text
text: Essential Services Being Well Maintained.

label: text
text: (British Wireless Service.)

label: text
text: Rugby, May 10.

label: text
text: No fresh development of the situation has occurred in any part

label: text
text: In particular the situation at the London docks and at other leading ports is well in hand. Supplies of light and power continue completely satisfactory, whilst the railway services show a progressive improvement. There is an abundant supply of volunteers, so that nearly 4,000 trains were running to-day.

label: text
text: The Government has practically completed a vast substitutional machine capable of maintaining the essential services of the community—railways, power, transport, and food supply.

label: text
text: Meetings of strikers passed off without incident, and the situation in London and the provinces is generally quiet. Where a few disturbances have occurred the civil police have quite successfully dealt with them.

label: text
text: Whilst many men are returning to work in different occupations there is no indication of any general movement in this direction. Reports from various parts of the country, however, say that there are signs of increasing anxiety amongst sections of the strikers on the constitutional issue, and that many workmen came out before realising that their action might reasonably be interpreted as "a challenge to the Constitution. A summing up of the reports would appear to indicate a general desire to re-establish the dispute on a purely industrial basis.

label: text
text: London's Buses

label: text
text: The omnibus services in London show a progressive improvement. The transport difficulties in many provincial towns are also being considerably reduced.

label: text
text: There is a normal train service in Liverpool and an efficient omnibus and train service in Edinburgh.

label: text
text: Tramway men have resumed work at Huddersfield, Dewsbury, Leeds, Bath, and other places, where the train services are now running.

label: text
text:
At Bath it is noteworthy that the men signed on as non-Unionists.
The omnibus systems in all counties south of Thames are running punctually, and the public are able, by catching connections, to make journeys of some length.
Overseas Passengers: Twenty-six ships were docked and undocked in Liverpool during the week-end and thirty to-day. The passengers arriving at this and other ports are being conveyed to their destinations without any delay unless they are bound for remote places. For instance, the liners Caronia and Baltic arrived at Liverpool to-day from New York Motor coaches were waiting to convey the passengers.
The Ballarat arrived at Plymouth from Australia and South Africa

label: text
text:
and her 450 passengers left immediately for London by special train.
Railway Activity.
Statements issued by two of the main railway systems illustrate to what extent the strike has been counteracted in regard to railway transport.

label: text
text: The London and North-eastern Railway announce that 1,000 trains are now working on their system as compared with 760 on Saturday. During the week-end 94 goods trains were worked, carrying milk, vegetables, fish, cattle, meat and general merchandise.

label: text
text: The London, Midland, and Scottish Railway announce that they are running about 1,000 passenger trains, and that this number will be increased to-morrow. They have been able to make such progress with the re-instatement of the passenger trains as to cover the essential sections of the railway with a service sufficient to meet requirements. They have, indeed, a surplus of passenger train staff for present requirements, and are turning their attention to the freight train services as the situation permits.

label: text
text: Stock Exchange

label: text
text: Whilst the Stock Exchange remained extremely quiet to-day a favourable tendency prevailed, and whatever changes took place were in a higher direction. Industrial notably were harder

label: text
text: The great milk depot which the Government has established in Hyde Park is now being supplied so freely by railway that supplies by road are being dispensed with, and the lorries so far used for this purpose are being diverted for the transport of flour, bacon, etc., from the docks and for other services.

label: text
text: Two hundred vessels, bringing 2,000 tons of fish, arrived at different ports to-day. Very reasonable prices are being maintained for fish.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER NEWS.

label: text
text: Serious disorders occurred at Glasgow over the week-end. Many shops were looted on Saturday morning, and conflicts with the police in the eastern district, particularly at Bridgeton, necessitated the rushing up of strong reinforcements.

label: text
text: The struggle was of the wildest, pots, pans, iron bars, pickheads and hammers being used. Fortunately, no police were injured. Sixty arrests were made.

label: text
text: Looting was renewed in the evening in the North, South, and West areas. Boot shops suffered most. Police and specials were hotly engaged until the early hours of Sunday morning. Many baton charges were made and there were 72 arrests.

label: text
text: There was fierce rioting in the Southern area, during which two constables and one special, who is a Greek, were hurt and sent to hospital.

label: text
text: The majority of the rioters were charged and sentenced to three months imprisonment.

label: text
text: At Lloyds cover against damage due to civil commotion is quoted at 2s. 6d. to 10s. 6d. per cent. Twenty-five guineas per cent. is quoted for insurance of pay of total loss in the event of the strike not being called off by the Trade Union Congress within four weeks from May 7; thirty guineas for three weeks, fifty for two and seventy-five for one.

label: text
text: Irish Trade Unionists have complied with the Trade Union Congress request to hold up food stuff shipments to Britain, and the port of Dublin is at a standstill. There are no cross-channel shipments whatever.

label: text
text: Prices of farm produce have considerably fallen. The Free State-English mails which reached Kingston on Friday night have since been held up owing to the dockers' refusal to handle them. Volunteers have now taken them.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOROCCAN WAR.

label: text
text: (Hasas Agency.)

label: text
text:
On Saturday evening French and Spanish troops made an effective junction on the slopes of Jebel Tunsi. The French have control everywhere in the Valley of Kert of which pacific occupation was refused by the Riffane at the conference of Udida, while Spanish progress continues favourably. The French have advanced twelve kilometres. Aeroplanes bombarded Targuist, where the Riffine fled in panic.

EGYPTIAN INDEPENDENCE
CAMPAIGN.

label: text
text: The Mixed Courts have, given judgment in the case of Mrs. Folk, widow of the American ex-Senator, who recently proceeded against Zagul Pasha and Mahomed Mahmoud Pasha claiming $600,000 for her husband's services in the cause of Egyptian independence.

label: text
text: The Courts rejected the claim against Zaglul and Mahmoud personally, but condemned Zaglul, as'resident of the Egyptian Wafd, o pay $55,000 with costs.

label: doc_title
text: POLAR FLIGHT

label: text
text: BYRD CLAIMS SUCCESS FIRST

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: A message to the "Times" from Spitzbergen says that Lieut. Byrd flew over the North Pole and returned safely to Spitzbergen after a flight lasting 15½ hours.

label: text
text: Coolidge Pleased

label: text
text: New York, May 10.

label: text
text: In a statement this morning President Coolidge expressed his heartliest congratulations in connection with Lieut. Byrd's Polar flight, adding that the fact that the flight seems to have been accomplished without mishap demonstrates the high development of the art in this country.

label: text
text: Lieut. Byrd sent a wireless message to his mother, who is living at Richmond, Virginia, announcing his safe return. His mother told Press representatives that she was "very proud of Dick".

label: text
text: Lieut. Byrd's brother, Mr. Henry Byrd, Governor of Virginia, expressed himself in like terms, adding that "Dick has been lucky all his life."

label: doc_title
text: DANISH FLIGHT.

label: text
text: LIEUT. HERSCHEND ARRIVES AT RANGOON.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Rangoon, May 10.
Lieut. Herschend has arrived

label: text
text: [A cable received on April 4 said:—The Danish aviator, Commander Botved, has arrived at Bangkok. The Danish airmen, Commander Botved and Lieut. Herschend left Copenhagen on March 17 on a flight to Tokyo and return, the route being via Berlin, Lemberg, Constantinople, Aleppo, Bombay, Calcutta, Hongkong, Shanghai and Peking. Herschend experienced engine trouble; and was forced to land with his machine damaged near Rangoon.]

label: text
text: COMMISSION PROCEEDING TO HANKOW.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Extrality Commissioners, who are visiting the provinces, will leave for Hankow by this evening's express.
A new stock has been received. Same prices offered.

label: text
text: On arrival here, the captain of the German steamer "Vogtland," from Miri on May 6, reports that the second cook died on board on Sunday of sunstroke, and was buried at sea.

label: text
text: For depositing refuse in the street, a servant boy in the employment of Major Fynch, of 2, Armend Building, was fined $5 at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning.
